name: Neck training harness

lead: A neck training harness is a head strap or cap, attached to a chain and weight plate, that loads the neck muscles through flexion, extension and side flexion. Wrestlers and fighters have long used it, and it has gained popularity among people seeking a thicker neck.
Proponents say a larger neck broadens the base of the head, affecting the silhouette and how the face and jaw sit in photographs.

paras: The neck muscles respond to loading like other muscles: progressive resistance, sufficient volume and recovery increase strength and size. Systematic reviews of neck exercise in people with neck pain show neuromuscular and strength adaptations, though no review focused on muscle thickness in healthy lifters was found, so the appearance claim rests on general resistance-training principles.

The cervical spine is vulnerable, so heavy loads, jerky reps and poor control risk strains and nerve irritation; guidance is to begin with very light loads and progress slowly. People with neck injury, disc problems or dizziness are advised to seek medical advice. Product claims about a thicker neck are plausible with months of training, but the evidence for lifters is indirect.
